scRNA-seq.sample_type: PBMCs and ACK-lysed/red blood cell-lysed whole blood peripheral immune cells
scRNA-seq.readouts: single-cell gene expression, cell-type proportions, differential gene expression, gene signature/module scores

evidence_location.quote: We saw similar trends in immune cell composition between the three modalities, including depletion of CD16 monocytes, dendritic cells (DCs), and NK cells, as well as increases in plasmablasts (PBs) in patients with severe and fatal COVID-19.

scATAC-seq.readouts: single-cell chromatin accessibility, TF motif accessibility/activity, accessibility at cytokine and CD4 regulatory loci

evidence_location.quote: Using chromVAR analysis to quantify TF activity from the chromatin accessibility of each cell, we found increased NF-κB activity in mild cases and significantly decreased activity in severe cases (P = 0.0047, Wilcoxon test; Fig. 5 C ; Schep et al., 2017 ).

CyTOF.readouts: single-cell protein expression and immune cell subset proportions

evidence_location.quote: Proteomic profiling of COVID-19 monocytes recapitulated many of our transcriptional findings ( Fig. 3, G–I ). This included a loss of CD16 + monocytes as well as a distinct shift in the phenotype of CD14 + monocytes.

bulk transcriptomic dataset.readouts: bulk gene expression signature score used to predict 28-d mortality

evidence_location.quote: We found that the developing neutrophil gene score accurately predicted 28-d mortality of the 17 patients who succumbed to infection (area under the curve, 0.81; Fig. 9, H and I ).
